title: Hockenheim: RL specialist (200M steps) vs the optimal lap
notes: Hockenheim is a development (R-dev) circuit; no lockbox circuit is used.

The optimum is the s-domain minimum-time OCP with continuous controls (T_cont), on the same vehicle ODE, car and corridor margin. It is not the CERTIFIED 20 Hz answer key T*_20 (TO-OCP lap mode is not built yet). T_cont <= T*_20, so this gap overstates the time left for a 20 Hz policy.
Agent: deterministic mean action, rolling start at s = 0, n = 0 at 90% of the QSS reference speed, lap 2 timed (the protocol of apexzero.eval.laps). Its lap time equals the harness's to 1.6e-04 s.
Sectors C1, C2, ... are corner complexes from apexzero.tracks.corners.segment plus half of each neighbouring straight; they are not official turn numbers.

t.description: time since the ghost crossed the start line

s.description: arc length along the reference line, 0 at the start line

n.description: lateral offset from the reference line, positive to the left

x.description: world x of the car's reference point

y.description: world y of the car's reference point

heading.description: yaw angle in the world frame, unwrapped (continuous)

steering.description: road-wheel steering angle (actuator state, after lag)

cmd_steer.description: steering command in [-1, 1] active from this sample on

cmd_pedal.description: pedal command in [-1, 1] (>0 throttle) active from this sample on

util_front.description: front-axle force demand / friction ellipse, before the tyre saturates (> 1: demand clipped back onto the ellipse)

util_rear.description: rear-axle force demand / friction ellipse, before saturation

ellipse_use.description: grip actually used on the busier axle, |F| / F_max after saturation (1 = at the limit)

meta.protocol: rolling start at s = 0, n = 0; deterministic mean action; lap 2 of 2 timed

meta.time_mapping: t(s) from the OCP's trapezoidal dt/ds; channels interpolated linearly in t onto a uniform 20 Hz grid
meta.control: continuous (piecewise linear in s), not the 20 Hz zero-order hold
